items.fact: Season window: season/itinerary.cal say Jul-Sep, but best_season/seasonal_guidance/pro_tips say the route is best (and conditions degrade badly by high summer) in Late May-early July
items.prior_evidence: The one source that states a window (a club route page: July, August) backs neither side exactly, and aligning best_season would need month-by-month guidance and pro tips that no source gives, so nothing is changed. Club route page for Mount Buckner North Face: 'Seasons: July, August'. The summit route page and its comment give no months; a guide service offers the peak March-October. PEAKBAGGER PASS: Still real; no peakbagger North Face ascent states a season window, so there is still no source for either side. Peakbagger ascent list for Mount Buckner shows about ten North Face entries (dated July, e.g. 2011-07-25 and 2020-07-19); the reports read carry only route names and gear, with no statement of when the face is in condition. Dates of individual ascents are not a stated window.

No source states a mileage from Whatcom Pass or Perfect Pass to a camp below Ghost Peak, so the waypoint (about 5 mi past Whatcom Pass) and itinerary day 3 (7.5 mi) cannot be reconciled. A 2016 Northern Pickets party (Crooked Thumb, Phantom, West Challenger) gives only hours and gain per day (Whatcom Pass knoll to the Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine 11.1 h, +3,700 ft) and a 54-mi whole-trip total; it states no leg mileage and did not climb Ghost. Peakbagger and summitpost are blocked and not archived for Ghost Peak. PEAKBAGGER PASS: Peakbagger lists only two Ghost Peak ascents and neither has a trip report or stats, so no stated mileage exists. Peakbagger ascent list for Ghost Peak: two ascents (one undated, one 1986), no trip reports, no gain or distance fields.

items.fact: Pass-to-summit distance: beta/pitch_detail 0.4 mi vs waypoint distMi 7.4 -> 8.5 (1.1 mi)
items.prior_evidence: No source states a mileage from Fish Creek Pass to the summit by the southeast ridge; sources give only vertical (about 1,000 ft) and time (45 min to an hour). The peak's route page describes the Southeast Ridge from Fish Creek Pass as about 1,000 ft vertical of class 2 with no distance (its '1 mile' figure is for the west ridge from the Oval Lakes side, a different line); a Bulger-list report gives 45 min to an hour from the pass; a regional hike guide gives 7.5 mi to the pass and nothing beyond it. PEAKBAGGER PASS: Peakbagger's short-leg figures for Courtney's SE/East ridge (0.9 mi, about 1,200 ft) start from a 7,191 ft point reached from Star Peak, not from Fish Creek Pass, so none states the pass-to-summit distance. Peakbagger 2026-06-07 SE Ridge ascent: 'Gain on way in: 1203 ft', 'Distance: 0.9 mi', 'Start Trailhead: 7191 ft', climbed second after Star Peak; 2012 East Ridge list entry 1,194 ft / 0.9 mi (also a second peak). Full-trail entries give 7.4-8.7 mi to the summit from the trailhead, nothing from the pass.

items.fact: Published approach time 4 hr vs itinerary 5-6 hr to Fish Creek Pass
items.prior_evidence: The stated trailhead-to-pass times (about 3 h and about 4 h) are both day-pack times and disagree; adopting 4 h in the overnight schedule would shift its later times and day total, which would have to be computed. A 2020 GPS-timed day party took 3 h 05 min to the pass and a 2023 day hiker about 4 h; no source times the pass with an overnight pack. timing.approachTimeHrs 4 matches one day-hike source, but the itinerary's '+5 to 6 hr' sits in a 32 lb backpacking schedule whose camp arrival (3:30-4:30 PM) and 9.5 h day follow from it, so changing it alone would create a new contradiction. PEAKBAGGER PASS: Peakbagger ascents are day trips that give whole-trip stats, not an overnight-pack time to Fish Creek Pass, so the 4 h tile and the 5-6 h schedule cannot be reconciled from a stated value. Peakbagger Courtney ascent list: trail ascents list 4,394-4,646 ft and 7.4-10.7 mi to the summit (e.g. 2022 'Fish Creek Pass' 4,394 ft / 7.4 mi) with no time to the pass; the 2026-06-07 report gives a 12 h 19 min car-to-car for a four-peak day.

cleared_value.notes: From the Argonaut-Colchuck col (~7,700ft) gain the east ridge crest over low-angle blocks and broken granite steps, easing into the climb before the terrain steepens.
Surmount a compact, steeper granite tower via face moves and thin gear placements; this is the route's technical crux and the most sustained pitch on the ridge.
Weave over and around a series of towers along the crest, alternating short exposed steps with easier ledge traverses; belay from a horn where the ridge narrows.
Moderate climbing and scrambling up blocky granite toward the upper mountain, with route-finding between minor gendarmes rather than sustained difficulty.
Continue past another gendarme on the upper ridge, staying near the crest on exposed but moderate granite before the angle relents toward the summit spires.
Class 3-4 ridge traverse to the base of the summit block, finishing with a short nonexposed scramble past the block's small cave feature to the true summit.
